description: Rust-native AI agent workspace built on adk-rust v0.6.0 with EverMemOS-compatible memory vault (Obsidian wiki 6-level hierarchy). Personal tool for daily software engineering with multi-provider LLM support, tool system, MCP, filesystem sandbox, and memory lifecycle.

userStories.title: Scaffold project with adk-rust
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to scaffold the project using cargo adk new and customize it for our harness with the correct source structure.
acceptanceCriteria: cargo adk new agent-harness creates correct project
cargo build passes with no errors

Custom source structure created: src/{main.rs, harness.rs, cli/, tools/{file.rs, shell.rs, search.rs, web.rs, memory.rs}, memory/{vault.rs, parser.rs, retrieval.rs, lifecycle.rs, types.rs}, context/, sandbox/, config/, providers.rs}
userStories.notes: Phase 1.1 — foundation for all other stories. Version updated to 0.7.0 (latest available).

userStories.title: Multi-provider LLM — configure and switch mid-session
userStories.description: As a user, I want to use adk-rust's built-in multi-provider support and switch between models mid-session via slash commands.
acceptanceCriteria: Use adk-model built-in providers: Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, Groq, Ollama + OpenAI-compatible presets
/model <name> slash command switches model mid-session (re-creates model instance)
Wrapper struct ProviderManager holds current model and allows hot-swap
userStories.notes: Phase 1.2 — depends on US-001. Uses adk-model providers + provider_from_env()

userStories.title: Built-in file tools using #[tool] macro
userStories.description: As an agent, I need file read/write/edit tools implemented using adk-rust's #[tool] macro.
acceptanceCriteria: FileRead tool using #[tool] macro with path and optional range parameters
FileWrite tool writes content to file
FileEdit tool performs string replacement in existing file (old_string to new_string)
All file operations scoped to working directory via sandbox (US-006)
userStories.notes: Phase 1.3 — depends on US-001. Uses #[tool] macro. Implemented with adk-tool 0.6 #[tool] macro, schemars for JSON Schema, thread-local sandbox context pattern, atomic writes, and path traversal protection.

userStories.title: Shell + Grep/Glob tools using #[tool] macro
userStories.description: As an agent, I need shell execution and file search tools with destructive command protection.
acceptanceCriteria: ShellExec tool using #[tool] macro: run shell command with timeout (default 120s)
Grep tool: search file content using grep-regex crate internally
Glob tool: find files by pattern using glob crate
Destructive command detection in ShellExec (rm -rf, git push --force, DROP TABLE, DELETE FROM, git reset --hard)
Return needs_approval: true flag for destructive commands, CLI prompts user before executing
! command shell escape in REPL: run directly without agent
userStories.notes: Phase 1.4 — depends on US-001. Uses #[tool] macro. Implemented ShellExec, Grep, Glob with destructive command detection and needs_approval flag. ! shell escape already wired in commands.rs.

userStories.title: Web search/fetch tools
userStories.description: As an agent, I need web search and URL fetching capabilities.
acceptanceCriteria: WebSearch tool: search via Serper.dev API or DuckDuckGo
WebFetch tool: fetch URL content, convert to markdown/text
Results returned as structured JSON (title, URL, snippet)
userStories.notes: Phase 1.9 — depends on US-001. Uses #[tool] macro. Implemented WebSearch (Serper.dev + DuckDuckGo fallback) and WebFetch (HTML to text/markdown) with rate limiting (10 req/min).

userStories.title: Filesystem sandbox & safety
userStories.description: As a user, I want all agent operations scoped to my project directory with approval prompts for dangerous actions.
acceptanceCriteria: Leverage adk-sandbox crate as base, extend with custom rules
Path scoping: all file ops restricted to working directory
.agentignore file support (use ignore crate, same format as .gitignore)
ToolConfirmationPolicy integrated with adk-rust's built-in HITL system
3 permission modes via .harness/settings.json or --permission flag: strict (default), auto, yolo
userStories.notes: Phase 1.5 — depends on US-003, US-004. Custom sandbox with .agentignore (ignore crate GitignoreBuilder), ToolConfirmationPolicy mapping, 3 permission modes. adk-sandbox not used (feature not enabled) — built our own layer that integrates with adk-rust's HITL.

userStories.title: Session persistence using adk-session
userStories.description: As a user, I want conversation history saved using adk-rust's built-in SQLite session backend.
acceptanceCriteria: Session metadata: project path, model, provider, timestamps
userStories.notes: Phase 1.6 — depends on US-001. Uses adk-session SQLite. Implemented SessionManager wrapping SqliteSessionService with create/list/get/delete/resume. /sessions and /resume slash commands wired. Auto-creates session on startup; --resume flag for CLI resumption.

userStories.title: Custom CLI REPL with slash commands
userStories.description: As a user, I want an enhanced REPL built on top of adk-cli with domain-specific slash commands.
acceptanceCriteria: Extend adk-cli or build custom REPL using rustyline
Streaming token output via adk-runner event streaming
! command shell escape: run shell directly
Colored output: tool calls (yellow), errors (red), success (green)
userStories.notes: Phase 1.7 — depends on US-002, US-005, US-006. Custom REPL using rustyline with streaming output, Ctrl+C cancellation, all slash commands, multi-line input (code blocks + backslash continuation), colored output, MoMo banner. Stub commands for /cost, /mem, /kms, /skill list, /mcp list (implemented in later stories).

userStories.title: One-shot mode
userStories.description: As a user, I want to run a single prompt and exit for scripts/CI.
userStories.notes: Phase 1.8 — depends on US-008. Uses adk-runner. Implemented one-shot mode with streaming output, stdin pipe support, proper exit codes (0 success, 1 error), tool calls to stderr, agent text to stdout.

userStories.title: AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md context injection
userStories.description: As a user, I want the agent to auto-discover project instruction files and inject them into the system prompt.
acceptanceCriteria: Walk up from cwd finding: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .harness/AGENTS.md
Read all discovered files, inject into system prompt via LlmAgentBuilder::instruction()
Files closer to cwd have higher priority (closer overrides further)
No files found → continue without error
userStories.notes: Phase 1.10 — depends on US-008. Uses LlmAgentBuilder::instruction(). Implemented directory-walking context discovery with relative path display and priority ordering. 9 new tests.

userStories.title: MCP integration using adk-tool built-in MCP support
userStories.description: As a user, I want to connect to MCP servers using adk-rust's built-in MCP client.
acceptanceCriteria: Use adk-tool MCP integration (stdio + HTTP Streamable)
MCP tools auto-registered with mcp_ namespace prefix
Support MCP Elicitation (servers can request user input)
userStories.notes: Phase 2.1 — depends on Phase 1 complete. Uses adk-tool MCP client. Implemented McpService wrapping McpServerManager with config persistence, /mcp add/list/remove commands, auto-start on harness build, graceful shutdown, elicitation handler, toolset registration with agent.

userStories.title: Memory vault — Write & Extract lifecycle
userStories.description: As an agent, I want to automatically create MemCells and extract Events/Foresights/Episodes after each conversation turn into the Obsidian wiki vault.
acceptanceCriteria: mem_write tool (#[tool] macro): append MemCell to daily log
mem_extract tool: extract events + foresights + episode from MemCells
ObsidianVault struct manages all vault I/O with vault_path, config, counters
Notes created following schemas in memory-vault/
userStories.notes: Phase 2.2 — depends on Phase 1. Main differentiator. Implemented mem_write/mem_extract/mem_read/mem_stats tools with #[tool] macro, ObsidianVault with daily log files, extraction engine (events/foresights/episodes), config persistence, index regeneration.

userStories.title: Memory vault — Retrieval (4 modes)
userStories.description: As an agent, I want to search my memory vault using multiple retrieval strategies.
acceptanceCriteria: mem_search tool with 4 modes: grep_llm (default), graph_walk, tag_filter, agentic
grep_llm: grep candidates → LLM rank → top N
tag_filter: filter by YAML frontmatter tags
agentic: multi-round grep → LLM sufficiency check → refined queries → merge
mem_read tool: read specific note by ID or wikilink
mem_graph tool: get connected notes (outgoing + backlinks)
userStories.notes: Phase 2.3 — depends on US-012. Uses #[tool] macro. Implemented 4 retrieval modes (grep_llm, graph_walk, tag_filter, agentic) with TF-IDF scoring, wikilink graph traversal, tag filtering, and multi-round query expansion. Added mem_search, mem_graph, mem_profile tools. 20 new tests.

userStories.title: Memory vault — Consolidation & Reflection
userStories.description: As an agent, I want to consolidate memories into clusters and update my profile over time.
acceptanceCriteria: mem_consolidate tool: cluster MemCells + update agent profile
Cluster detection: same project + overlapping keywords (threshold: 0.65)
Profile compaction: when items > 37 → LLM consolidates to ~17
userStories.notes: Phase 2.4 — depends on US-013. Uses #[tool] macro. Implemented mem_consolidate (Jaccard similarity clustering, profile operations with ADD/UPDATE/DELETE, compaction at 37 items), mem_validate_foresights (expired pending foresights), mem_reflect (weekly/monthly). 14 new tests.

userStories.title: Skill system using adk-skill
userStories.description: As a user, I want to use adk-rust's built-in skill system (SKILL.md parsing + discovery) with custom skill installation.
acceptanceCriteria: Use adk-skill crate for SKILL.md parsing + whenToUse matching
Auto-match: adk-skill matches user request via lexical matching
/skill install <git-url> custom command: clone + install skill
userStories.notes: Phase 2.5 — depends on Phase 1. Uses adk-skill 0.7.0 via adk-rust skills feature. SkillService wraps SkillIndex with discovery from .skills/, .claude/skills/, .harness/skills/. /skill list and /skill install implemented. Auto-match via select_skills(). Skill context injected into system prompt.

userStories.title: Sub-agent orchestration using adk-agent
userStories.description: As an agent, I want to delegate subtasks to isolated sub-agents using adk-rust's built-in agent types.
acceptanceCriteria: Use SequentialAgent and ParallelAgent from adk-agent
Task tool: delegate subtask → spawn sub-agent with own tool registry
Recursion limit: 3 levels deep (enforced by runner config)
Sub-agent reports back as structured result
userStories.notes: Phase 3.1 — depends on Phase 2. Uses SequentialAgent / ParallelAgent

userStories.title: Knowledge base (KMS)
userStories.description: As a user, I want a project wiki that the agent can search on demand.
acceptanceCriteria: KmsRead tool: read a KMS page
KmsSearch tool: full-text search across KMS pages
KmsWrite tool: agent creates/edits KMS pages
KMS TOC injected into system prompt every turn
userStories.notes: Phase 3.2 — depends on Phase 2. Uses #[tool] macro

userStories.title: Secrets management — OS keychain
userStories.description: As a user, I want API keys stored in OS keychain instead of .env files.
acceptanceCriteria: Keys NEVER written to config files or logs
userStories.notes: Phase 3.3 — depends on Phase 1. Custom implementation

userStories.title: Streaming & cancellation (enhance adk-runner defaults)
userStories.description: As a user, I want real-time token streaming and cancellation.
acceptanceCriteria: Partial response saved to session on cancel
Graceful shutdown: finish current tool call before exit
userStories.notes: Phase 3.4 — depends on US-008. Uses adk-runner events

userStories.title: Cost tracking
userStories.description: As a user, I want to track token usage and costs across sessions.
acceptanceCriteria: Token counting per request (input + output) from adk-runner events
Cost estimation using adk-anthropic pricing data (extend to all providers)
Cost data persisted in session DB
userStories.notes: Phase 3.5 — depends on US-007, US-019. Uses adk-anthropic pricing data

userStories.title: Agent teams (multi-process coordination)
userStories.description: As a user, I want multiple agents working in parallel using adk-rust's ParallelAgent + A2A protocol.
acceptanceCriteria: Use adk-server A2A v1.0.0 for inter-agent communication
Lead agent spawns worker agents as separate processes
Each worker in own tmux pane + optional git worktree
Merge coordination: lead merges branches when workers done
userStories.notes: Phase 3.6 — depends on US-016. Uses adk-server A2A v1.0.0
